Definition: from G3326 and G3725; bounded alongside, i.e. contiguous (neuter plural as noun, frontier):--border.
BiblicalUsage: Jesus went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, seeking a quiet house where no one would know Him, but He could not be hid. The word is the borderland itself, the edge where one country meets another, and it stands in the Received Text where the older Greek reads simply the region.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the borderland suits this story: Jesus crossed into Gentile country and could not be hidden, because even at the edges of the map, His fame went ahead of Him.
